requirement: A refused Joomla import sign-in says Joomla needs the username, not the email; the operator signal records whether the username was an email and how the run came in, never the value

oracle.ref: PR #1506 (fix); fix evidence: A production Joomla customer's import stopped on invalid_credential (Joomla: 'Username and password do not match'); the customer most likely typed the email address, which Joomla's backend does not accept, and the sentence did not say so
oracle.invariant: S1: Joomla gets import_error_invalid_credential_joomla; WordPress keeps import_error_invalid_credential; message_unread stays import_error_signin_unclear; no_backend_access keeps its own sentence. S2: the wizard shows the Joomla sentence. S3: diagnostic is {at: login_post, check: invalid_credential, username_is_email: true|false}; the queued report carries sign_in: password beside that detail; neither the run state nor the report contains the username. S4: only invalid_credential and no_backend_access gain username_is_email; owner@localhost is not an email shape; signInWay returns password, code, saved. S5: a boolean username_is_email survives, everything else (including sign_in, which belongs to the result) is dropped; importSignIn keeps only password/code/saved; the alert ends with 'Sign-in: password · username is an email address' and contains no @. S6: the queued report carries sign_in saved and no detail; the stored site.stuck row keeps sign_in and has no detail, its alert ends 'Reason: call_failed\nSign-in: password' with no Where line; an unknown sign_in is not stored; the site.result row keeps sign_in.
oracle.productSourceGap: no product file is imported, read or run through a supported form in the command's test files (see tests/qa/layers/unit/lib/sources.mjs)
